why: No standalone ICT-strategy instrument text was retrievable; this is the ministry's own dated statement confirming the Politique nationale du numerique (2021-2030) remains the operative reference framework and that it is being actualised, the clearest current-position statement available.
The most advanced in-window milestone toward a successor strategy: the 11 March 2026 national validation workshop for the PNDN 2026-2035 and its PSDN 2026-2030 sectoral plan.
A distinct, earlier event: the 13 October 2025 handover of the completed draft PNDN 2026-2035 to the minister, dating the point at which the successor's drafting phase closed.

No standalone national broadband strategy was located; this is the most recent authoritative ministerial statement of current position, covering backbone modernisation, the near-complete Tier III data centre and DTS phase 2.
The ministry's own account of the 14 November 2025 provisional reception of DTS fibre-optic sections, the period's central completed infrastructure milestone.
A distinct governance event: the 13 March 2026 DTS steering-committee session that adopted the 2026-2027 work programme and budget, separate from the fibre reception itself.

No separate cloud/data-storage strategy exists; this ministerial statement at the DTS fibre reception ceremony is the clearest dated confirmation of the national Tier III data centre's existence and then-current (under-construction) standing.

Sofrecom's own account of completing the feasibility study (sizing, design, site selection, tender preparation, cloud business plan) that let government proceed to tender -- a distinct design-phase milestone.
A distinct, later procurement step: ANSI's World Bank-financed tender for data-centre infrastructure equipment, issued 4 February 2026.

The founding statute: Article 35 institutes Niger's Referentiel General d'Interoperabilite and Articles 29-33 enable inter-administration electronic exchange; the ministry's own official page for the law, captured in full.

The 18 May 2026 Council of Ministers' adoption of the decree fixing interoperability mechanisms between the civil-status and population registers -- the clearest in-window legal movement on interoperability.
A distinct, later operational milestone: the 11 August 2026 launch of the RNP enrolment information campaign, moving the May decree from text to rollout.

No adopted AI strategy instrument was located; this is the government's own dated statement (29 July 2025) that it intends to elaborate a national AI and data-management strategy, establishing the strategy's pre-adoption standing.
The 23 September 2025 national colloquium whose recommendations were stated to feed directly into the national AI strategy -- a distinct expert-input event in the formation process.
A distinct, later event: ANSI's participation in the January 2026 Dakar AI capacity-building workshop, including direct exchanges on AI-strategy development with Senegal's digital ministry.
Niger's only existing data-localisation rule: Article 47 of the consolidated data-protection law requires identifiable health data to be hosted on national territory.
The operative cross-government data-protection law and the HAPDP's enforcement mandate; the closest instrument to a general data-governance framework that was located.
The 18 May 2026 decree governing management and exploitation of the national civil-status and population registers -- data governance exercised over the state's core identity data.
A distinct, earlier institutional step: the 22 April 2026 creation of the ANEI, the agency now tasked with governing biometric registration and identification data nationally.
Niger's only general access-to-public-information instrument, establishing a right to public information and administrative documents including free electronic delivery.
A dated publication of a new government dataset: the 13 May 2026 handover of the INS household ICT-access survey, distributed to ARCEP and Teledistribution du Niger.
A distinct, earlier open-data-portal launch: the 18 September 2025 relaunch of the INS-hosted PNIN nutrition-data portal as an interactive data library.
Niger's dedicated cybercrime statute, the founding/enacting act; the ministry's own official page for the law.
The 11 October 2025 Council of Ministers' creation of the Centre National de Cybersecurite (CNAC), operationalising the 2022 national cybersecurity strategy institutionally.
A distinct, later legal-reform event: the Justice Ministry's 17 April 2026 statement that the new Penal Code introduced new cybercrime provisions.
The operative regional instrument governing payment services for banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions across UMOA, binding Niger as a member state.
BCEAO's own notice of the 30 September 2025 official launch of the UEMOA-wide instant-payment platform (PI-SPI) that Niger's banks connect to under this regime.
A distinct, later rollout-status event: BCEAO's 2 April 2026 communique reporting 80 live PI-SPI participants and setting a 30 June 2026 connection deadline for all supervised institutions.
The same founding statute as the governance-chapter interoperability indicator: Article 35's Referentiel General d'Interoperabilite is the enabling legal instrument.
The primary legislative act in the window: the 22 April 2026 ordonnance reforming the civil-status regime and creating the ANEI to remedy the registers' lack of interoperability.
The implementing decree, a distinct later step: the 18 May 2026 decree specifying the interoperability mechanisms the April ordonnance required.
